stem: In the C4 model, which diagram shows the system as a box within its users and the other systems it interacts with?

options.text: Code diagram
System context diagram
Component diagram
Container diagram

explanation: C4 has four levels: context, containers, components and code. The context diagram shows scope and external actors and systems.

stem: When presenting an architecture recommendation to executives, what should come first?

options.text: A detailed component list
The decision required, the options considered, the recommendation, and the cost, risk and benefit in business terms
The technology history
The deployment scripts

explanation: Executives need the decision, the trade-offs and the business impact. Detail can follow for those who want it.

stem: Which is the best way to hand a design from architecture to the delivery team?

options.text: A single verbal briefing
A written handoff with scope, key decisions and their reasons, interfaces, non-functional requirements, risks and open questions
Only the slide deck used for sales
A list of vendor names

explanation: A written handoff makes the decisions and constraints explicit and carries the reasons so the team can handle unexpected cases.

stem: A client's CTO receives an 80-page architecture document and says nobody will read it, yet the steering committee must approve funding next week.

options.text: Prepare a short decision pack: one-page context and reference architecture, the two or three key decisions with options and a recommendation, risks and costs, with the long document as an appendix.
Send the 80 pages again with a cover note.
Present only high-level slides without options or risks.
Ask the committee to read the document in the meeting.

rationales.text: The audience needs decisions and trade-offs, not every detail.
Completeness of documentation is what committees want.
Keeping the long document as an appendix preserves traceability.
Omitting risks makes approval easier and is acceptable.

explanation: Tailor communication to the decision: concise decisions and trade-offs up front, detail available on request. Omitting options and risks undermines trust.
model_answer: Create a short pack with context, key decisions, options, recommendation, risks and costs; link or append the full document.

stem: Two teams disagree on whether a new AI service should directly access a customer database. Each draws a different diagram and meetings go in circles.
constraints: Boundaries of the system are unclear

options.text: Agree a context diagram first (users, the AI service and external systems), then a container diagram showing data stores and interfaces, and use them to decide the access boundary explicitly.
Let each team present its own diagram again.
Vote on the diagram style.
Delay until a tool is purchased.

rationales.text: A shared, structured notation exposes the disagreement about boundaries.
Repeating separate diagrams will converge the views.
Layered diagrams separate scope questions from internal design.
Tooling choice is the root cause of the disagreement.

explanation: A shared notation at the right level makes assumptions visible and lets the group decide boundaries explicitly.
model_answer: Draw context then container diagrams jointly, mark the contested interface, and record the decision with reasons.
